perguntas.a: Yes. VulnexusAI is free, requires no signup and does not store data from scanned websites.

perguntas.q: How are the score and grade calculated?
perguntas.a: The result combines every category (HTTPS, headers, email DNS, cookies, CORS, sensitive files, content and infrastructure). The score goes from 0 to 100 and the grade from A to F, with a higher weight for the most critical items.

perguntas.q: Is my history stored on the server?
perguntas.a: No. Recent history is stored only in your browser, in localStorage, and is never sent to the server.

perguntas.q: Does the result replace a professional assessment?
perguntas.a: No. The check is fully automated and should be a starting point. For deep audits, consult a professional or complementary scanners.

sobre.metaDescription: Meet VulnexusAI and the free website security checker: what it does, what it doesn''t do and how it works.
sobre.resumo: VulnexusAI builds security tools for the web. This is one of them: free, simple and transparent.

secoes.p: The VulnexusAI checker is a free tool that analyzes a public website and generates an automatic score. It checks HTTPS and SSL certificates, security headers, email DNS (SPF, DMARC and DKIM), cookies, sensitive files, content and infrastructure.
Type the URL of a website and the tool runs a series of automated checks, showing a score from 0 to 100, a grade from A to F and fix tips for each item analyzed.
The scan is 100% automated with no human analysis — results in seconds, but not a professional assessment. Use the result as a starting point to dig deeper into your site's security.
Checks happen at the moment you type the domain. The URL is processed by the server to generate the scan and history is stored only in your browser. We do not store scan data.

seguranca.metaDescription: VulnexusAI vulnerability disclosure channels and how we handle security reports.
seguranca.resumo: Found a vulnerability in VulnexusAI? Thank you! Here is how to report it safely and what happens next.

secoes.p: Be objective: include the affected URL, step-by-step reproduction and estimated impact. Do not test beyond what is necessary, do not access third-party data and do not disclose publicly before a fix.
We acknowledge your report, analyze it, fix the issue and get back to you. We do not offer bug bounty rewards.
The dedicated email channel is being set up. In the meantime, the official contact point is this page, referenced in our security.txt file at /.well-known/security.txt.
This page covers the vulnexusai.com website and the checking tool. Vulnerabilities in sites checked by the tool should be reported to the owners of each site.

privacidade.metaDescription: Learn how the free VulnexusAI security checker handles data: the URL you check, browser-only history and functional cookies.
privacidade.resumo: This page describes, transparently, what data is processed when you use the security checking tool.

secoes.h: What we process when you check a website
secoes.p: The URL you type is sent to our server only to generate the scan (HTTPS connection, headers, certificate, DNS, cookies and sensitive files). It is not stored in a database.
Recent history is stored only in your browser, in localStorage, and is never sent to the server. Clearing your browser data removes this history.
To prevent abuse, the server temporarily limits the number of checks per IP address, keeping this control in memory. It is not persisted and is not used to identify or track users.

We use only functional cookies: one to remember your language preference and a technical session cookie used to apply security headers. We do not use tracking, advertising or third-party analytics cookies.
The check queries public services of the website itself (such as DNS and public files). The optional Google Safe Browsing check, when enabled, sends only the checked domain.
This policy may be updated as the tool evolves. Relevant changes will be reflected on this page.

termos.metaDescription: Terms of use of the free VulnexusAI website security checker: acceptable use, limits and disclaimer.
termos.resumo: By using the security checking tool, you agree to these terms.

secoes.p: Use the tool to check domains you own or are authorized to check. Do not use the tool to scan third-party websites without permission.
To protect the service, we apply a temporary limit of checks per IP address. If the limit is reached, you will see a notice with the time to try again.
The tool is provided as is, for educational purposes. We do not guarantee complete accuracy of the checks or the absence of errors.
Decisions made based on the score or the results are your responsibility. VulnexusAI is not liable for damages arising from the use of the tool or from decisions based on its results.
Use of the tool is free. We do not sell the checked data or use it for commercial purposes.

cookies.metaDescription: Cookie policy of the VulnexusAI security checker: only functional cookies, no tracking.
cookies.resumo: This tool does not use tracking cookies. Here is exactly what exists.

secoes.p: When you switch the site's language, a cookie stores your preference for future visits. We also set a technical session cookie used to apply security headers such as Content Security Policy. Neither collects data for profiling.
We do not use advertising cookies, third-party analytics cookies, tracking pixels or marketing services.
Your check history is stored in the browser's localStorage — local storage on your device that is not sent to the server and is not considered a cookie.
You can clear cookies and local data through your browser settings at any time. This does not stop you from using the tool; it only removes the language preference and local history.

vsSecurityHeaders.resumo: SecurityHeaders.com has been a trusted reference for checking HTTP security headers since 2014. VulnexusAI covers that same ground and adds SSL/TLS, email DNS, cookies, exposed files, and continuous monitoring — all in one scan.

vsSecurityHeaders.ctaTexto: No need to choose — VulnexusAI's check is free and takes seconds.

vsSslLabs.metaTitle: VulnexusAI vs SSL Labs — which to use? | VulnexusAI
vsSslLabs.metaDescription: Honest comparison between VulnexusAI and SSL Labs (Qualys): TLS analysis depth, response time, and what each tool covers.
vsSslLabs.resumo: SSL Labs, by Qualys, is the reference for deep TLS/SSL analysis — it simulates dozens of browser/client combinations and details certificate chains, ciphers and known vulnerabilities. VulnexusAI takes a broader approach: a fast overall security snapshot of a site, including what SSL Labs doesn't cover.

tabela.eles: Can take a few minutes — simulates dozens of client/browser combinations
Extremely detailed — full chain, ciphers, known vulnerabilities

vsSslLabs.veredictoTexto: If you need a deep, focused audit of a server's TLS configuration, SSL Labs is unmatched. For a fast overview — TLS, headers, email DNS, cookies and exposed files together — VulnexusAI covers more ground in the same check. Many teams use both: VulnexusAI day-to-day, SSL Labs for occasional deep TLS audits.
vsSslLabs.ctaTexto: No need to choose — VulnexusAI's check is free and takes seconds.

https-ativo.descricao: The website must respond over HTTPS to encrypt traffic.

detalhe.falha: The website did not offer HTTPS.

https-ativo.dica: Set up a TLS certificate (Let''s Encrypt, Cloudflare or your provider) and serve the site over HTTPS only.

redirect-http.descricao: HTTP visits should be automatically redirected to HTTPS.

detalhe.aviso: No automatic redirect detected in the chain.

redirect-http.dica: Configure a 301 redirect from http:// to https:// on the server or hosting platform.

certificado.descricao: The certificate must be valid, not expired and issued by a trusted authority.

detalhe.autoassinado: Self-signed certificate — browsers will show a warning.

certificado.dica: Renew the certificate before it expires or switch to one issued by a trusted authority (Let''s Encrypt).

tls-versao.descricao: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are obsolete and should be disabled (deprecated in 2020).
tls-versao.dica: Disable TLS 1.0/1.1 and keep TLS 1.2 and 1.3 enabled on the server.

hsts.descricao: HSTS — forces HTTPS connections and prevents downgrade attacks.
hsts.dica: Add `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains` to every HTTPS response.

csp.descricao: CSP — controls which resources the browser is allowed to load.
csp.dica: Define a CSP policy (e.g. `default-src 'self'`) and adjust it to your site's resources.

xframe.descricao: Prevents the site from being displayed inside third-party iframes (clickjacking).
xframe.dica: Add `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN` (or use the frame-ancestors CSP directive).

xcontenttype.descricao: Prevents the browser from MIME sniffing.

referrer.descricao: Controls which information is sent in the Referer header.

permissions.descricao: Limits access to browser APIs (camera, GPS, etc.).
permissions.dica: Add a `Permissions-Policy` restricting geolocation, camera, microphone, etc.

spf.descricao: SPF — authorizes which servers can send email on behalf of the domain.

detalhe.sem-email: Domain without MX — the site doesn't use its own email; SPF doesn't apply.

spf.dica: Publish a TXT record such as `v=spf1 include:_spf.provider ~all` in the domain DNS.

dmarc.descricao: DMARC — policy for handling emails forged with your domain.

detalhe.sem-email: Domain without MX — the site doesn't use its own email; DMARC doesn't apply.

dmarc.dica: Publish a TXT record at `_dmarc.domain` (e.g. `v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:your@email`) and strengthen the policy later.

dkim.descricao: DKIM — digital signature that validates the authenticity of emails.

detalhe.sem-email: Domain without MX — the site doesn't use its own email; DKIM doesn't apply.

dkim.dica: Set up DKIM with your email provider and publish the public key at `selector._domainkey.domain`.

mta-sts.descricao: MTA-STS — policy that enforces TLS for email delivery.

detalhe.sem-email: Domain without MX — the site doesn't use its own email; MTA-STS doesn't apply.

mta-sts.dica: Publish a TXT at `_mta-sts.domain` like `v=STSv1; id=20240901; mx: your-mx; mode: enforce` and host the policy at `/.well-known/mta-sts.txt`.

cookies.descricao: Session cookies should use security attributes.

detalhe.ok: No cookie set in the response chain.

cookies-secure.descricao: Cookies should only be sent over HTTPS.

cookies-httponly.descricao: Prevents cookie access via JavaScript (mitigates XSS).
cookies-httponly.dica: Add `HttpOnly` to cookies that don't need to be read by JavaScript.

cookies-samesite.descricao: Limits cookie sending on requests from other sites (CSRF).

safe-browsing.descricao: Checks if the site is listed on Google's malware and social engineering lists.

detalhe.ok: No threats listed on Google Safe Browsing.
detalhe.sem-chave: Optional check — Google Safe Browsing API key not configured.
detalhe.ameaca: The site is listed on Google Safe Browsing threat lists.
detalhe.sem-conexao: Could not query Google Safe Browsing.

dica.ameaca: Review the site in Google Search Console (Security and manual actions) and request re-evaluation.

cors-wildcard-credentials.descricao: Combining Access-Control-Allow-Origin with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is a dangerous configuration.
cors-wildcard-credentials.dica: Never combine Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. Restrict allowed origins explicitly.

cors-origin-reflection.descricao: The server should not reflect back any Origin header it receives.

detalhe.aviso: The server reflected the sent origin ({valor}).
detalhe.ok: The server does not reflect the sent origin.

cors-origin-reflection.dica: Configure a fixed allowlist of origins instead of reflecting the Origin header.

cors-wildcard-publico.descricao: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * without credentials is acceptable for public resources.

detalhe.ok: Open CORS ({valor}) — acceptable for public resources.

cors-wildcard-publico.dica: For public resources without credentials, a wildcard is acceptable.

cors-nao-configurado.descricao: No CORS headers configured — the browser's secure default behavior.

detalhe.ok: No CORS headers — the browser applies the default policy (no cross-origin access).

cors-nao-configurado.dica: Configure CORS only if the site must be accessed from other origins.

cors-indisponivel.descricao: Could not assess the CORS configuration.

detalhe.aviso: Could not verify the CORS headers.
